_about: Company / fund facts for the holding detail modal. Only sourced facts: descriptions paraphrased from the Webull company profile (stocks) or TradingView fund data (ETFs); EPS/revenue actual vs estimate from the Webull earnings calendar (latest reported quarter); next report date from the TradingView earnings calendar (confirmed=false means the company has not confirmed it). ETFs have no earnings. Missing = omitted on the page. Refresh: re-pull with Webull get_company_profile / get_stock_earnings_calendar and TradingView mcp-tv-get-earnings-calendar after any holding reports, and set asOf. 'about' rewritten 2026-11-02 in plain English: what the company does and how it makes money (well-known public facts; no figures).

VOO.name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF
VOO.about: A fund that tracks the S&P 500 index, so one share owns a slice of about 500 of the biggest US companies. Vanguard runs it and charges a small yearly fee; you make money when those companies grow and pay dividends.

VXUS.name: Vanguard Total International Stock ETF
VXUS.about: A fund that tracks the FTSE Global All Cap ex US index: thousands of companies in Europe, Asia and emerging markets, everything except the US. It spreads your money outside the US in one purchase.
VXUS.tracks: FTSE Global All Cap ex US

SCHD.name: Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF
SCHD.about: A fund that tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 index: about 100 US companies with a long record of paying and raising dividends. It pays out cash dividends every quarter.

BND.name: Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF
BND.about: A fund that tracks the Bloomberg US Aggregate Float Adjusted index: thousands of US government and company bonds. It earns money from the interest those bonds pay, and usually moves much less than stocks.

XLV.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund
XLV.about: A fund that tracks the S&P Health Care Select Sector index: the health care companies in the S&P 500, such as drugmakers, insurers and medical device makers.

AVUV.name: Avantis U.S. Small Cap Value ETF
AVUV.about: An actively managed fund (it doesn’t copy an index) that buys small US companies whose shares look cheap compared with their profits and assets, a style called small-cap value.

INDA.name: iShares MSCI India ETF
INDA.about: A fund that tracks the MSCI India index: the large and mid-size companies listed in India, such as banks, tech services firms and energy companies.

IAU.name: iShares Gold Trust
IAU.about: A fund that holds real gold bars in vaults and tracks the LBMA Gold Price PM index, so its price follows the price of gold. It pays no dividends.

ITA.name: iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense ETF
ITA.about: A fund that tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Select Aerospace & Defense index: US companies that build military equipment, jet engines and passenger planes.
ITA.tracks: Dow Jones U.S. Select Aerospace & Defense

SMH.name: VanEck Semiconductor ETF
SMH.about: A fund that tracks the MVIS US Listed Semiconductor 25 index: 25 of the biggest computer-chip companies, such as NVIDIA, TSMC and Broadcom.

GRID.name: First Trust Nasdaq Clean Edge Smart Grid Infrastructure Index Fund
GRID.about: A fund that tracks the NASDAQ OMX Clean Edge Smart Grid Infrastructure index: companies that build and upgrade the electric grid, such as power equipment, cables and meters.
GRID.tracks: NASDAQ OMX Clean Edge Smart Grid Infrastructure

NLR.name: VanEck Uranium and Nuclear ETF
NLR.about: A fund that tracks the MVIS Global Uranium & Nuclear Energy index: uranium miners, nuclear power plant owners and companies that build nuclear equipment.

DTCR.name: Global X Data Center & Digital Infrastructure ETF
DTCR.about: A fund that tracks the Solactive Data Center REITs & Digital Infrastructure index: companies that own data centers and cell towers and rent the space to tech and phone companies.
DTCR.tracks: Solactive Data Center REITs & Digital Infrastructure

UNH.name: UnitedHealth Group
UNH.about: The biggest US health insurer. It makes money from the premiums employers, people and the government pay for UnitedHealthcare plans, and from Optum, which runs clinics, health data services and a pharmacy-benefits business.
UNH.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

RTX.name: RTX
RTX.about: An aerospace and defense company. It makes money selling jet engines (Pratt & Whitney) and airplane parts (Collins Aerospace) to airlines and plane makers, plus missiles and defense systems (Raytheon) to the US and allied governments, and it earns more servicing engines after they are sold.
RTX.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

LLY.name: Eli Lilly
LLY.about: Eli Lilly is a drug company. It makes money selling prescription medicines, mainly Mounjaro and Zepbound for diabetes and weight loss, plus cancer and other drugs, to pharmacies, hospitals and insurers.
LLY.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

ISRG.name: Intuitive Surgical
ISRG.about: Intuitive Surgical sells da Vinci robots that help surgeons operate through small cuts. It makes most of its money after the sale: hospitals buy new instruments for every surgery and pay for service contracts.
ISRG.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

V.name: Visa
V.about: Visa runs the network that moves money when you pay with a Visa card. It doesn’t lend money itself; it charges banks and merchants a small fee on each purchase that goes through its network.
V.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

NVDA.name: NVIDIA
NVDA.about: NVIDIA designs the chips that train and run AI. It makes most of its money selling those chips and networking gear to cloud companies and data centers, plus GeForce graphics cards for gaming PCs.
NVDA.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

AVGO.name: Broadcom
AVGO.about: Broadcom designs chips used in data centers, networks, phones and AI systems, including custom AI chips built for big tech companies. It also sells software that large businesses pay for by subscription (it owns VMware).
AVGO.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

TSM.name: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC)
TSM.about: TSMC is the world’s biggest contract chipmaker. Companies like Apple and NVIDIA design chips, and TSMC gets paid to manufacture them in its factories, mostly in Taiwan.
TSM.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

MSFT.name: Microsoft
MSFT.about: Microsoft makes money from subscriptions to Office (Microsoft 365), renting computing power and AI through its Azure cloud, Windows licenses, LinkedIn, search ads and Xbox gaming.
MSFT.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

VRT.name: Vertiv
VRT.about: Vertiv makes the power and cooling equipment data centers need to keep servers running and from overheating. It sells that gear to data center builders and cloud companies, then earns more servicing it.
VRT.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

GEV.name: GE Vernova
GEV.about: GE Vernova builds the machines that make electricity, such as gas turbines and wind turbines, plus equipment for the power grid. It sells them to utilities and earns steady money from long service contracts.
GEV.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

CEG.name: Constellation Energy
CEG.about: Constellation Energy owns the largest fleet of nuclear power plants in the US. It makes money selling the electricity they generate to utilities, businesses and data centers, often on long-term contracts.
CEG.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)

CCJ.name: Cameco
CCJ.about: Cameco is one of the world’s biggest uranium miners. It makes money selling uranium and nuclear fuel to power plants, and it co-owns Westinghouse, which builds and services nuclear reactors.
CCJ.source: Webull company profile + Webull earnings calendar; next date from TradingView earnings calendar (2026-11-01)
